topic: sealed UKI VM test lanes for Secure Boot end-to-end proof of immutable OS images

subtopics.scope: Unified Kernel Image structure (PE sections: .osrel, .cmdline, .linux, .initrd, .splash), building UKIs with ukify and mkosi Format=ukify, and signing them for Secure Boot with PKCS#11 URIs pointing at PIV slot 9c or a SoftHSM emulation.

mkosi output format uki secure boot signing pkcs11

subtopics.scope: systemd-sbsign as the Secure Boot signing tool with the engine:pkcs11 private key backend, its contrast with legacy sbsigntools/sbverify, and signing against a SoftHSM-emulated PIV slot 9c in CI.
seed_queries: systemd-sbsign versus sbsigntools sbverify secure boot signing

subtopics.scope: Running signed UKIs in QEMU with OVMF Secure Boot: pflash code and VARS volumes, enrolling the platform root of trust (ROTPK) into the db allowed-signatures store, q35 machine with smm, and asserting SecureBoot=yes from systemd-stub.

QEMU UEFI secure boot test systemd-stub SecureBoot yes

subtopics.scope: TPM2 in VMs via swtpm socket passthrough, the sha256 PCR banks used at boot (PCR0 firmware, PCR4 boot manager, PCR7 Secure Boot policy, PCR11 kernel and initrd), what systemd-stub measures into each, and tpm2_pcrread golden-value assertions.
seed_queries: swtpm qemu tpm2 measured boot PCR values linux
systemd-stub PCR 11 kernel initrd cmdline measurement TPM

subtopics.scope: dm-verity root hash binding for immutable images: mkosi Verity=yes embedding roothash= in the UKI cmdline, composefs digest binding in BLS entries (composefs=sha512), and kernel-side tamper rejection when the store hash mismatches.
seed_queries: mkosi verity dm-verity roothash kernel cmdline
composefs fs-verity digest binding bootc immutable root

subtopics.scope: Sealing LUKS2 volumes at install time: systemd-cryptenroll with FIDO2 (hmac-secret, user verification uv=on), --unlock-key-type=fido2, TPM PCR-bound LUKS2 slots as the complementary primitive, and asserting the sealed slot via systemd-cryptsetup status.

Why the sealed Secure Boot VM lane is its own CI workflow rather than a step in the unsealed bootc-filesystem lane: failure-class isolation, dependency footprint, staged evidence plan (unsigned first, then seal, then negative tamper assertions enforced).
